newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil eases again after fall.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil eases again after fall.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil prices were weaker on Friday, adding to the week's falls, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $103 and $104 fob ARA, compared to deals as high as $111 on Thursday. Dealers attributed this to poor bunker demand and good supply.
Cargo prices had fallen to barge levels on Thursday amid talk of fresh transatlantic avails heading this way, and dealers said prices had failed to rise above barges on Friday.

Confirmation came on Friday from Russian state oil holding firm Rosneft that Russia would not impose an export duty on fuel oil this winter but NWE traders said they doubted this would have much of an impact on prices as dealers in the market already thought it unlikely such a duty would be imposed.
Russian supplies were thought thin for the moment, although mild weather in the Baltics meant export barrels would find passage to NWE easy.
Low sulphur markets were wallowing at lower levels, with February swaps talked at around $108 fob NWE. Supply remains long.
